problem: The sentence "taskset -c 0 make runs make only on CPU 0" is garbled: "make" appears twice and reads as if the command runs itself. A phone reader will stall on it.
fix: taskset -c 0 make runs the program make only on CPU 0, because taskset -c 0 restricts the process it launches to CPU 0.

problem: The answer contradicts itself and the section. It first says "no other CPU touches that copy", then says "without this, another CPU could see or change it". A per-CPU copy is never touched by another CPU; the real danger of leaving preemption on is that the task can migrate between reading the CPU number and using the copy, so it operates on the wrong CPU's copy.
fix: Each CPU has its own copy of the variable. With preemption disabled the task cannot migrate, so the copy it reads or writes is always the one belonging to the CPU it is running on. Without that, the task could be moved to another CPU between taking the CPU number and the access, and would then touch a different CPU's copy while that CPU is using it.
